what: Kids and Car Safety documents vehicle-related injuries and promotes education, safer vehicle design, and policy changes.
Its work includes hot-car deaths, backovers and frontovers, entrapment, submersion, and support for affected families.
A hot-car-only working estimate is about $920,000 per 10 USA QALYs, with very wide uncertainty about influence, adoption timing, and funding additionality.
strengths: Detecting an unattended child and triggering timely rescue is a concrete, credible route to preventing death.
Technical studies show why simple door-based reminders leave gaps that better detection and alerts could address.
The recipient operates at a small reported budget and has a sustained, focused presence in a broader safety coalition.
reservations: No field study establishes the organization’s marginal effect on fatalities, rule timing, or device adoption.
Existing industry innovation, government work, slow fleet turnover, and inaccessible older vehicles limit the additional benefit.
Financial reserves include a material cryptocurrency holding, and the latest located return is unaudited cash-basis reporting rather than a current operating plan.

sections.what:
[Kids and Car Safety](https://www.kidsandcars.org/) collects incident information, distributes safety education, supports affected families, and advocates for vehicle design and policy changes. Its [program history](https://www.kidsandcars.org/accomplishments-and-history) includes national Look Before You Lock materials and a Kansas/Missouri Childproof Your Ride initiative, alongside work on entrapment, vehicle submersion, frontovers, and carbon monoxide. This review assesses ordinary support to Kids and Cars Inc, EIN 20-0024715—not purchase of a child detector or a restricted hot-car campaign.

All reported recipient costs are charged. Only prospective hot-car mortality prevention is quantified; pets, other injury mechanisms, nonfatal morbidity, and family wellbeing are not automatically converted into QALYs. Past safety standards are not credited again to new support.
sections.monitoring:
The organization’s [incident database](https://www.kidsandcars.org/hot-cars/media-resources) is useful for identifying scenarios and affected families, but documented cases are not a controlled estimate of prevented deaths. Changes in reporting, annual weather, exposure, and technology adoption can change counts without measuring charity impact. [NHTSA reports 31 deaths in 2025](https://www.nhtsa.gov/campaign/heatstroke), while its technical report describes a historical average near 37 annually.

The [2026 regulatory agenda](https://www.reginfo.gov/public/do/eAgendaViewRule?pubId=202510&RIN=2127-AM49) still places the rear-designated seating-position alert rule at prerule stage and lists a July 2026 planned advance notice; a scheduled date is not evidence of completion. The mandate to issue a rule is not an implemented universal direct-detection standard. Some secondary summaries describe universal alerts in 2025; this review does not rely on that characterization.

Better monitoring would connect risk-weighted vehicle penetration, system activation, false alarms, timely rescues, and adoption changes attributable to KACS. Brochures, media impressions, and coalition participation alone cannot establish those links.
sections.qualitative:
The mechanism does not require a charity-specific randomized trial to be plausible, but it does require more than a sensor detecting movement. [NHTSA tested 12 door-logic systems](https://rosap.ntl.bts.gov/view/dot/79012/dot_79012_DS1.pdf); none could alert when a child independently entered an unlocked vehicle, and some scenarios produced no alert. [Transport Canada’s testing](https://tc.canada.ca/en/road-transportation/dangers-hot-vehicles-children/technical-report-testing-occupant-monitoring-systems) favored radar with strong alerts over simpler systems. Its full report was available only by request, so this review uses the published summary and does not invent measured accuracy.

[CHOP researchers](https://injury.research.chop.edu/blog/posts/new-research-evaluates-technological-solutions-prevent-pediatric-vehicular-heatstroke) examined 354 fatal cases and 10 exemplar scenarios. No single technology covered every scenario; alert recipients still had to intervene. This is retrospective scenario analysis, not a real-world mortality-effect estimate. I therefore use separate subjective detection, timely rescue, and operating-reliability factors rather than calling theoretical coverage lives saved.

I judge a small positive marginal influence plausible given KACS’s sustained focus and [documented collaboration](https://www.safekids.org/national-heatstroke-prevention-day-press-release). My central opinion credits KACS 20% of a hypothetical 20-percentage-point coalition-induced chance of accelerating stronger protection: an effective4-percentage-point contribution before donor substitution. Zero remains entirely possible.

The CHOP source here is the investigators’ public research summary; journal full text was inaccessible. No unreported field-effect coefficient is attributed to it.
sections.cost:
The hot-car working estimate is approximately **$920,000 per 10 USA QALYs**. Favorable assumptions give about $38,000; a low-influence scenario exceeds $4.9 billion, with zero and negative outcomes also shown. These are broad subjective scenarios, not confidence bounds or a claim that the expected value is a likely realized outcome.

The model asks whether stronger detection and rescue systems arrive three years earlier than otherwise. It slowly ramps additional protection across the at-risk vehicle population, discounts annual benefits, and allows baseline adoption to catch up. It does not presume every vehicle changes immediately or that KACS is responsible for all future hot-car prevention. The [industry’s pre-existing commitment](https://www.autosinnovate.org/posts/press-release/2024-industry-heatstroke-report) and already-available systems are part of the counterfactual.

About 0.52 discounted expected deaths averted under the full five-year cost-equivalent central model, at 27 QALYs per death, produces about 13.94 USA QALYs. The death-to-QALY value is a judgment based on a long remaining lifespan with annual discounting, not 80 undiscounted healthy years. Other portfolio health is assigned zero net credit, not assumed proven harmless.

The donor-facing cost excludes manufacturers’ incremental hardware and public implementation costs. Because the alternative also adopts later, the incremental social cost is the extra cost of acceleration or stronger features—not necessarily the entire eventual hardware bill. A current social-cost estimate remains unavailable.
sections.funding:
The [FY 2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202513039349301566/IRS990) reports $256,454 expenses: $179,537 program, $27,906 management, and $49,011 fundraising. This is cash-basis reporting; the return says statements were not independently audited or reviewed. [FY 2023](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202420799349301032/IRS990) requires adding $4,517 direct fundraising-event cost to $258,364 functional expenses, for $262,881 gross. FY 2022 expenses were $265,887. The three-year mean is $261,741.

FY 2024 revenue was $597,894, including $323,028 noncash support and $21,003 government grants. [Schedule M](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202513039349301566/IRS990Schedule M) identifies a $300,000 cryptocurrency donation. [Schedule D](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202513039349301566/IRS990Schedule D) records $303,125 in Coinbase/Bitcoin at year end; this is not its present market value. Cash and savings totaled $167,395, versus $428,767 net assets overall. Donor restrictions are not separately classified under this reporting presentation; none are assumed freely spendable merely from net assets.

The [ordinary giving page](https://kidsandcars.networkforgood.com/projects/140012-kids-and-car-safety) illustrates $50 for materials reaching 500 families. That is not full recipient cost per family or a proven health return. Staff/consultant and volunteer capacity, future reserve use, and replacement donors determine what additional support changes. The central 50% additionality is an opinion over five years, not an observed staffing commitment.

Scenario G=$10,000 is disclosure normalization only. Unpriced volunteer time and hardware/government implementation costs are not claimed included in reported cash expenses; those are separate resource/capacity uncertainties.
model.geographicAttribution: National US prevention pathway with g=.99 subjective allowance for exact 50states+DC boundary and exposure coverage. State education remains charged even when not modeled. No pet QALYs or foreign beneficiaries are credited. allPopulationQalys covers this quantified pathway before g, not complete worldwide organizational impact.
model.formula: F1(t)=min(cap,rate*max(0,t-L1+1)); F0(t)=min(cap,rate*max(0,t-L0+1)); A=sum(t=1..T)[F1(t)-F0(t)]/(1.03^t). H=D*d*r*k*q*A. Q_USA(G)=G/(Y*C)*b*(p*a*H-h)*g. Central: C256454,Y5,D30,d.8,r.7,k.9,q27,b.5,p.2,a.2,rate.05,cap.8,L1=3,L0=6,T20,g.99,h0. Price10*G/Q_USA. Adoption paths are risk-weighted fractions of otherwise-fatal exposures receiving stronger protection, not observed shares of cars sold.
model.counterfactual: Existing government campaigns, simple reminders, manufacturer innovation, other charities and eventual stronger detection continue. Central compares the same adoption ramp beginning in future year3 rather than6; it credits temporary earlier coverage, not permanent prevention of all baseline deaths. D30 incorporates a modest decline from historical37 deaths, close to recent31, rather than projecting an immutable historic rate.
model.attribution: p=.2 is a subjective coalition-induced chance of the specified three-year acceleration; a=.2 is KACS’s share of that causal increment. Effective contribution .04 is not the chance any regulation happens. b=.5 then discounts effort that reserves, government/private grants, or other donors would fund anyway. All portfolio costs are charged, so no second hot-car budget share is applied.
model.uncertainty: Working expected value, not an experimentally estimated charity return or a median realized policy outcome. Adoption and causal attribution dominate; broad scenarios include no acceleration, no influence, funding substitution, and adverse net health elsewhere. h is not discounted by policy success, preserving downside even when p=0.
model.nativeOutcomes: Risk-weighted vehicle-years with stronger child detection; successful detection; functioning alert; timely rescue; deaths prevented. Theoretical scenario coverage, education materials, and historical laws are not treated as measured fatality reductions.

what: The Berkeley Center for Independent Living helps people with disabilities live in their communities.
It provides equipment loans and repairs, home-access support, peer programs and other services in Northern Alameda County.
An ordinary gift supports the recipient’s broad services; the quantified estimate below covers repair and loaner benefits only.
strengths: Repairing a mobility device or removing a home barrier can change daily function directly.
The residential-access page identifies a real geographic funding limitation rather than only asserting general need.
Current accounts and primary studies permit separating recipient costs, public funding and plausible health pathways.
reservations: No current completed-repair volume, marginal cost or delay-reduction evaluation was identified.
An equipment loan may bridge days before an insured repair rather than create years of new mobility.
The full recipient includes advocacy, training and support whose marginal health returns differ from equipment services.

sections.what:
CIL serves Northern Alameda County residents through a broad independent-living portfolio. It is the Berkeley charity with EIN 23-7175191, not the similarly named Corporation for Independent Living at cil.org. Its current service pages offer loans of wheelchairs, ramps and other equipment as inventory permits, with a repair-request route. This is evidence of delivery capability, not an assured inventory or turnaround time. [Current programs and Northern Alameda County service area](https://thecil.org/) [Assistive technology loaners and repairs](https://thecil.org/assistive-technology/at-loaners-and-repairs/)

Home-access work includes modifications such as ramps and grab bars. Berkeley's publicly funded program is distinct from nearby cities, where CIL says lack of funding limits it to consultations. A gift might enable otherwise-unfunded modifications, but no priced expansion plan establishes that an unrestricted gift would go there. [Residential access and geographic funding gap](https://thecil.org/residential-access/)
sections.monitoring:
The most useful repair measure is additional person-days with a safely functioning device compared with the actual alternative: vendor repair, insurance, another loaner, self-repair or going without. Record request and completion dates, device fit and use, recurrent failures, outside repair availability and resulting health/function. Repeat repairs for one person must not each receive an entire lifetime benefit. [Assistive technology loaners and repairs](https://thecil.org/assistive-technology/at-loaners-and-repairs/)

The attendant registry prioritizes high-risk people when provider supply is scarce. Matching information is not itself paid care, filled hours or prevented institutionalization. CIL should measure additional sustained care hours and health outcomes, including cases where the limiting resource is a worker rather than coordination money. [Personal attendant services and limited provider registry](https://thecil.org/core-services/personal-attendant-services/)

Original returns provide financial detail but broad, partly historical program descriptions rather than current cohort outcome data. The audit index flags FY2023/FY2024 internal-control weaknesses. The underlying audit download was unavailable in this review, so neither the exact finding nor its resolution is independently established here; this is a follow-up item, not a finding of fraud. [Filing and audit index](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/237175191)

The [city’s draft FY2025 CAPER](https://berkeleyca.gov/sites/default/files/documents/DRAFT_COB_PY24%20CAPER_SAGE_0.pdf) reports seven CIL-supported rental accessibility projects. These are publicly supported outputs, not additional donor-caused health.
sections.qualitative:
A multicenter observational wheelchair study found frequent repairs and adverse consequences, including being confined at home; another reported median repair time of 14 days. These document a meaningful problem, but they do not estimate the causal effect of CIL repair or a health-utility decrement. Vendor users may differ in severity, device complexity and resources. [Factors influencing wheelchair repairs and consequences](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8501145/) [Wheelchair repairs: delays, causes and associated outcomes](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39427781/)

Other branches have credible external evidence. The HIPI randomized home-modification trial estimated an adjusted reduction in home fall injuries, with a crude estimate whose interval included no effect. Its New Zealand households and modification package are not interchangeable with CIL's client mix or every ramp installation. [HIPI home modification cluster-randomized trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25255696/)

Living Well was evaluated with a randomized wait-list design in 246 consumers across independent-living centers. Results support some improvement in secondary conditions and health-related outcomes. The investigators' later synthesis says symptom days returned to baseline by twelve months and health costs by two months; neither perpetual savings nor lifelong QALYs are justified. CIL currently offers the curriculum, but delivery fidelity, additional enrollment and local results remain unknown. [Health promotion: evaluation of Living Well with a Disability](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17032708/) [Living Well with a Disability: intervention and follow-up synthesis](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/65/su/su6501a10.htm) [Living Well Senior Program](https://thecil.org/core-services/living-well-senior-program/)

Independence, access and dignity are important even when incompletely measured by QALYs. Disability status is not a discount on a person's worth; any quantitative benefit should be a change in their experienced health or function, not an assumption that disability makes a life less valuable.
sections.cost:
A limited-pathway conditional estimate is about **$59 million per ten California QALYs** from additional repair/loaner capacity, with the costs of the ordinary recipient gift retained. This is not a measured CIL result or a comprehensive estimate of its other programs. The native bridge is staff time and materials → completed appropriate episodes → otherwise-lost functional days restored. Those uncertain steps are now stated numerically rather than hidden behind a break-even threshold.

The central scenario allocates 10% of an ordinary gift to this capacity. It assumes a $34 hourly wage, 35% employment loading, four staff hours and $100 materials per attempted episode, then applies the latest recipient total/program cost ratio of 1.588 for support. The wage is a rounded proxy from a [current CIL specialist vacancy](https://jobs.gusto.com/postings/center-for-independent-living-inc-community-independent-living-specialist-e3d951ce-6b3c-4e55-b1bf-48c31cc1a655), not a repair-technician quote; the other service inputs are judgments. This produces about $450 per attempted episode. Financing/capacity replacement halves delivery; 80% completion/fit and 50% improvement over equivalent alternatives reduce it further.

For a truly additional episode, the scenario assumes a 0.10 health-utility improvement for fourteen otherwise-lost days, beginning after a quarter-year implementation delay, discounted at 3% annually. Fourteen days is a transfer assumption, not CIL's measured acceleration. CIL's [current month-long response queue](https://thecil.org/assistive-technology/) is actually longer than the external survey's median completed-repair time, so alternative services must be checked. Favorable and adverse joint assumptions span roughly $272,000 to $1.82 trillion per ten QALYs, with zero additional gain also possible. These are stress scenarios, not confidence bounds. They show how little a short repair-acceleration model can establish about the full recipient's return. Home access, transition support, health education, advocacy and other effects may dominate and remain unestimated; their value is not asserted to be zero.
sections.funding:
Original returns report full-recipient expenses of $2,986,495 (FY2023), $3,662,458 (FY2024) and $4,370,584 (FY2025), all June-ending twelve-month periods. The three-year mean is $3,673,179. FY2024 functions were $3,017,406 program, $644,978 management and $74 fundraising. [Original FY2024 Form 990 with FY2023 comparative totals](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/237175191/202521359349306602/full)

FY2025 expenses split into $2,752,037 program, $1,362,449 management and $256,098 fundraising. Revenue was $3,996,267, including $3,223,822 government grants and $349,468 other contributions. Compensation and benefits totaled $3,219,987. The operating deficit was $374,317; net assets were $7,809,089, of which $2,385,204 carried donor restrictions. Net assets are not all immediately available cash. Functional allocations changed substantially; they are accounting categories, not measures of effectiveness. [Original FY2025 Form 990, IRS electronic filing](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/237175191/202641359349312384/full)

CIL says services are free and supported by government, foundations and individuals. Publicly funded Berkeley modifications, insured equipment alternatives and other donors all matter to substitution. A reported funding gap outside Berkeley is promising but does not price the ordinary-gift margin. The general donation page supports the broad portfolio and includes optional designated routes; this report assumes no designation and records no actual donation. [Eligibility, free services and funding](https://thecil.org/about-us/faq/) [General donation route](https://thecil.org/donate/)

CIL's [current careers page](https://thecil.org/job-listings/) posts a $28/hour starting-pay floor and benefits, while the [AT page](https://thecil.org/assistive-technology/) seeks skilled repair and preparation volunteers. These support a labor-capacity pathway but do not prove that cash is the binding constraint or that a donation funds a new position.

model.costScope: Ordinary unrestricted gift, C=$100,000 analytical normalization. Full gift remains charged even though this model quantifies only a repair/loaner health pathway. f is an explicit marginal portfolio allocation, not a restricted donation. Unit cost k includes wages, employment loading, materials and allocated recipient support. This is donor-dollar cost, not a societal-cost estimate; donated device and partner resource opportunity costs remain unknown.
model.geographicAttribution: g_CA=1 for the short-duration direct-service scenario, based on Northern Alameda County eligibility. National advocacy benefits are not counted. This is an inference about weeks of local client benefit, not location of headquarters.
model.formula: k=(w*b*h+p)*o USD per attempted repair/loaner episode. N=C*f/k*m*s*a additional successfully restored-function episodes, where m is financing/capacity additionality, s is fit/completion success, and a excludes otherwise equivalent timely alternatives. q=du*exp(-r*L)*(1-exp(-r*D/365))/r for D days gained beginning L years after gift. Q_all=N*q; Q_CA=g_CA*Q_all; price_10_CA=10*C/Q_CA if positive. Each episode is counted only for the actual counterfactual interval with lost function; sum person-days without overlaps and no repeated lifetime award. Other CIL channels remain unestimated.
model.counterfactual: CIL's existing grants, payroll and inventory, insured/vendor service, publicly financed device loan centers, Easy Does It emergency repair and individual backups continue. A donor-funded slot must actually accelerate restoration relative to these options. CIL's current month-long response queue is NOT itself the number of functional days lost or saved.
model.attribution: m discounts replacement of grant/reserve funding or staffing constraints; a separately discounts equivalent alternative repair/loaner service and usable backups. s accounts for failed or unsuitable delivery. Do not count one disability-related utility improvement separately as avoided injury, isolation and mobility restoration. No attribution of all recipient work to the repair branch.
model.uncertainty: A bottom-up subjective conditional central, not a measured CIL effect and not a comprehensive estimate of every recipient benefit. Wage and organization support scale have source anchors; allocation, labor time, materials, completion, substitution and health gain are judgments. Favorable/adverse scenarios are simultaneous stress tests, not confidence limits. Zero and harms are not excluded. Omitted institutional-transition, access, counseling, education and rights benefits could materially change a full-portfolio estimate; this partial model should not be read as proof of a poor overall return.
model.nativeOutcomes: Central at C=$100,000: $10,000 of modeled portfolio allocation; 22.203 gross attempted slots at k=$450.39279; 11.101 after financing/capacity adjustment; 8.881 completed appropriate episodes; 4.441 that beat an equivalent alternative; 62.168 otherwise-lost functional person-days regained. With du=0.10, finite duration and start delay this produces 0.01689533 California QALYs. No episode, day or utility value is an observed CIL outcome.

inputs.rationale: 35% benefits/payroll/paid-leave loading; CIL advertises extensive benefits but actual marginal load is unreported. Stress 1.2–1.5.

inputs.name: h
inputs.rationale: Intake, handling, repair or loaner preparation, fitting and closeout combined. No local time-motion study; stress 2–8 hours.

inputs.name: p
inputs.rationale: Average repair/cleaning/component allowance, not device retail price or CIL observed invoice. Stress $50–500; actual case mix could exceed this.

inputs.name: o
inputs.rationale: Central proxy equals observed total/program expense ratio 1.5881269; applying average support loading to marginal service cost is a judgment. Stress 1.3–2, not an accounting confidence bound.

inputs.name: m
inputs.rationale: Half the modeled allocation adds usable service capacity after grant/reserve replacement and staffing constraints. Public grants are large, while requests and volunteer needs suggest unmet demand. Stress 0.1–0.8 plus zero.

inputs.name: s
inputs.rationale: Repair/loaner can fail or be unsuitable. External SCI repair survey's completion data motivate uncertainty, not a measured CIL success rate. Stress 0.5–0.95.

inputs.name: a
inputs.rationale: Half successful episodes deliver function otherwise lost after allowing insurance/vendors, state loan centers, EDI and backups. Stress 0.1–0.9.

inputs.name: D
inputs.unit: functional days gained per truly additional episode
inputs.rationale: Finite acceleration prior, not observed days saved. External survey median repair duration was 14 days; CIL reports roughly one month before responding, so its current service is not automatically faster. Stress 2–60 days.

inputs.name: du
inputs.rationale: Assumed health-related change from restored appropriate mobility function; not a valuation of the person's life. Stress 0.02–0.2. Does not monetize independence, rights or all social benefits.

inputs.name: L
inputs.rationale: Central quarter-year implementation/queue delay; stress 0.05–0.5.

inputs.name: r
inputs.rationale: Explicit convention; survival set to one over at most 60 days with no mortality gain claimed.

inputs.name: g_CA
inputs.unit: California share of short direct health gain
inputs.rationale: Local client eligibility and short horizon; no nationwide spillover credited.

inputs.name: incremental partner/device opportunity cost
inputs.rationale: Donated equipment, public loan shipping, external repair and any public costs induced by expansion not measured.

scenarios.label: No added function
scenarios.assumptions: m=0, a=0 or D=0: funding substitution, equal alternative service or no acceleration. No finite positive cost-per-QALY.

sensitivity: Central partial-health price is about $59 million per ten California QALYs, favorable about $272,000 and adverse about $1.8 trillion. These joint stress scenarios are not confidence limits.
Halving f, m, s, a or du halves modeled QALYs. Doubling episode cost k doubles price. Longer counterfactual loss, not a longer loan recorded on paper, is needed to increase D.

At central delivery yield, reaching $1 million per ten QALYs requires roughly 59 times more health gain than the 14-day repair scenario supplies. Substantially longer unresolved access problems or separately demonstrated benefits from other programs could alter that assessment.
Current CIL response time is longer than the external median completed-repair time. Replacing D with that queue length without checking alternatives would overstate donation impact.
Home modifications are not added merely because a ramp is durable. Public funding substitution, who would otherwise remain without access, severity and duration are separate unresolved inputs.
The model's high partial-pathway price is not an estimate that unmodeled CIL services provide no value. Preserve this scope warning beside any displayed number.

Marginal third-party resource cost and current audit/control remediation evidence.

what: Comité Cívico del Valle works on health and environmental conditions in Imperial Valley.
Its portfolio includes asthma home visits, air monitoring, heat work, community relief and energy-related advocacy.
This evaluates the California health return of an ordinary recipient gift rather than assuming it buys only asthma services.
strengths: Direct home visiting and local exposure work offer identifiable routes to better health.
The organization participated in a local comparative study, providing unusually relevant evidence to challenge generic claims.
Original accounts and an identified public asthma grant clarify recipient scale and funding substitution.
reservations: The local study found no statistically detected effect of the randomized family intervention at twelve months.
Asthma was a small reported expense category; the unrestricted portfolio is much broader.
Monitoring, environmental review and education require additional implementation before they yield measurable health benefits.

sections.what:
CCV's current site describes seven initiatives spanning public health, environmental justice and energy transition. The asthma program offers bilingual home education, trigger identification and self-management support; it identifies CalEPA funding. This is not a clinic that independently supplies all medication and medical care. [Current initiatives and organization](https://ccvhealth.org/) [Current asthma intervention and management](https://ccvhealth.org/asthma-intervention)

The same recipient operates air monitoring and broader community programs. Its air-quality page describes California work alongside collaborations in Canada and Mexico, so an unrestricted gift's California benefit share cannot simply be assumed to be 100%. Direct Imperial Valley care is California-scoped; cross-border and national effects require separate attribution. [Air-quality network and monitoring initiatives](https://ccvhealth.org/air-quality)
sections.monitoring:
For home visiting, useful measures are additional completed patient courses beyond public funding, changed medication/trigger management, and symptom-free days measured against usual care. Track baseline severity, actual visit dose, dropout, seasonal change and recurrence. For monitoring, the key bridge is how information changes exposure: implemented controls or protective behavior, duration, uptake and alternative data sources. A monitor reading alone is not avoided illness. [Current asthma intervention and management](https://ccvhealth.org/asthma-intervention) [Air-quality network and monitoring initiatives](https://ccvhealth.org/air-quality)

Current heat work is described as a community research and mitigation initiative with San Diego State University. The reviewed page does not supply a completed counterfactual evaluation or a priced unfunded intervention. General community relief may reduce hardship, but distributed items cannot be converted directly into health gain. [Taking on the Heat initiative](https://ccvhealth.org/extreme-heat) [Share and Care](https://ccvhealth.org/share-and-care)
sections.qualitative:
The most directly relevant evidence is Respira Sano, conducted with CCV in 400 Imperial County youth. Assignment to family home visiting was randomized; clinic exposure depended on where children received care. The investigators found no statistically detected effect of the family intervention at twelve months. Fewer unplanned visits in the clinic comparison cannot be credited to CCV home visits, and clinic selection was not randomized. All groups received community intervention, so its independent effect was not identified. Missing process data and imperfect lung tests limit interpretation. This does not prove today's program has zero benefit, but it is substantial counterevidence to an automatic positive transfer. [Respira Sano primary comparative-effectiveness report, April 2021](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK599376/)

A separate Seattle randomized trial found 2.10 more symptom-free days per two weeks after CHW home visits versus usual care, with a 95% interval of 1.17–3.05. Different targeting, service dose and existing care may explain differing results. The trial's symptom-day outcome is not a QALY measure; caregiver quality-of-life scores and avoided visits cannot simply be added as QALYs. [Randomized home visits for Medicaid-enrolled children with asthma](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26270287/) [CDC Medicaid Asthma Home Visit Project registry](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02258308)

CCV's August 2026 account reports an appellate decision requiring further environmental review of a lithium/geothermal project, particularly water and Salton Sea air-quality issues. I verified the organization's statement, not the original opinion's full contents. Improved review is not yet a measured reduction in dust exposure. Any health model must compare actual mitigation with the project and energy alternatives that would otherwise occur, including harms from delay or substitution. Coalition work with Earthworks cannot all be assigned to a marginal CCV gift. [CCV reports lithium-project environmental review appeal](https://ccvhealth.org/news/california-court-of-appeal-orders-imperial-county-to-correct-major-environmental-deficiencies-in-hells-kitchen-lithium-project-approval)
sections.cost:
The central cost per 10 California QALYs is unestimated. We have relevant causal evidence and original costs, but the additional ordinary-gift service mix, funded capacity and local health effect remain unidentified. A favorable external asthma trial does not identify the health return of the much larger outreach and policy portfolio.

An explicit finite clinical sensitivity gives a useful hurdle. If the Seattle endpoint difference of 2.10 symptom-free days per fourteen days held throughout one full year, and each gained symptom-free day improved health utility by an illustrative 0.10, q = (2.10/14) × 0.10 = 0.015 QALYs per additional patient-year. Full-year persistence is optimistic relative to an endpoint measurement; the 0.10 mapping is judgment, not trial data. A linear rise from zero to that effect over the year halves q. No mortality, second year or separate urgent-care benefit is added. [Randomized home visits for Medicaid-enrolled children with asthma](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26270287/)

At q = 0.015, reaching $1 million per 10 QALYs requires 66.667 additional California patient-years per $100,000, or at most $1,500 of whole-recipient gift cost per effective patient-year. A $100,000 threshold requires 666.667 patient-years, or $150 each. Those are break-even requirements, not predictions. Under a purely diagnostic assumption that the gift follows the FY2024 asthma expense share (1.928%), allowable asthma-branch cost per effective patient-year falls to $28.93 or $2.89 respectively. Historical share is not a measured marginal allocation; the calculation demonstrates why restricted-program efficiency cannot stand in for recipient efficiency.

Other branches could add substantial benefit, but require independent finite models of implemented exposure changes, incremental public action or delivered care. Overlapping respiratory benefits must be combined at person level, not counted once for asthma visits and again for air-quality work.
sections.funding:
Original returns report full-recipient expenses of $3,025,205 in 2022, $4,652,438 in 2023 and $6,458,632 in 2024, giving a three-year mean of $4,712,092. The 2023 return provides the 2022 comparative total; these are accrual, calendar-year accounts rather than a cost per participant. [Original FY2023 Form 990 with FY2022 comparative figures](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/330411322/202403199349314080/full)

In 2024 total expenses comprised $4,513,451 program, $1,926,502 management and $18,679 fundraising. Reported program categories included $4,047,828 community outreach, $341,076 air monitoring and $124,547 asthma services. Revenue was $5,727,894, including $1,591,989 government grants and $4,044,851 other contributions. Net assets were $4,766,066, with $1,025,820 donor-restricted. Expenses include $831,661 depreciation; donor cash expenditure and economic resource cost should not be silently conflated. [Original FY2024 Form 990](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/330411322/202533189349315318/full)

CalEPA awarded $300,000 in 2024 for at-home asthma education and intervention in Imperial Valley. Current program text still identifies that funding. The award establishes an existing financed pathway, not remaining cash, a current shortfall or a gift-induced expansion; spending timing and restrictions must be checked. [CalEPA announces EJ Action Grants including CCV asthma project](https://calepa.ca.gov/2024/03/07/blog-ej-action-grants-announcement/)

The current action page links to a petition, not a verified ordinary-donation checkout. The relief page invites financial support for its program, but that is not enough to identify an unrestricted donation route. The report therefore leaves donationUrl null pending verification rather than directing a user to an assumed or restricted destination. No donation or endorsement is claimed. [Current action page, petition rather than donation form](https://ccvhealth.org/take-action) [Share and Care](https://ccvhealth.org/share-and-care)

model.costScope: Full ordinary-recipient gift, including outreach, air/energy work, asthma and support. $100,000 is only arithmetic normalization. Public grants and donated resources are not purchased anew by every gift; social resource cost is separate.
model.geographicAttribution: Direct Imperial County asthma benefit is in California. The ordinary portfolio includes cross-border collaborations, so marginal California share is unknown; threshold cases explicitly require California-resident patient-years.
model.formula: Q_CA(C)=Σ_j N_j,additional(C, allocation, public-funding substitution)×∫Δu_j(t)S_j(t)g_CA,j(t)(1+r)^−t dt + joint policy/exposure benefit − harms. Asthma sensitivity q=(2.10 symptom-free days/14 days)×0.10 utility×1 year=0.015 QALYs; N_required=10C/(target cost per10Q×q). Historical-share diagnostic: f=124547/6458632; branch cost ceiling=f×q×target/10.
model.counterfactual: Existing CalEPA-financed visits, ordinary clinical asthma care, regulators' monitoring and project review, other environmental groups and alternate energy supply continue. A new gift must change service or implementation, not merely accompany it. The local trial compared family visits within a common community intervention.
model.attribution: No arbitrary coalition fraction or historical win credit. Separate gift-to-capacity, completed uptake, clinical effect and California beneficiary share. For policy, identify incremental implementation probability and finite exposure change; combine overlapping health trajectories.
model.uncertainty: Central effect unknown. Local randomized family-intervention findings challenge positive generic transfer. Break-even cases are conditions, not expected yield or probability bounds. Null/negative net effects remain possible, especially with implementation failure or policy tradeoffs.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional completed asthma courses and symptom-free patient-days beyond usual care; Measured exposure reductions caused by implemented controls or behavior; Avoided illness attributable to actual heat mitigation, not training counts

reports.program: Prescription hearing-aid access, professional fitting and student support

acceptance.evidence: docs/geography-access-batch-five-acceptance.md; independent Medium audit plus root review; research only.

what: Help America Hear connects financially eligible people with donated prescription hearing aids and professional fitting services across the United States.
Its program covers moderate to profound hearing loss and includes limited follow-up, while patients still face evaluation, accessory and possible fitting costs.
The charity also provides student scholarships; the health case rests on sustained hearing and communication improvements rather than the retail value of devices or scholarships.
strengths: Hearing aids have a direct, testable clinical mechanism, with randomized US evidence of sustained improvement in communication.
Professional fitting and a last-resort financial screen can target people whose needs are not met by standard insurance or inexpensive retail devices.
The small recipient reports actual fitted people and modest reserves, permitting concrete per-case and funding-capacity tests.
reservations: No public current waiting-list, manufacturer quota or provider-capacity budget establishes how many extra completed fittings a donation buys.
Hearing-specific benefits are clearer than generic QALY gains, and long-term use or replacement is not tracked publicly for this recipient.
Full costs include substantial fundraising events and scholarships; eligibility fees, care access and an unresolved registration data flag warrant follow-up.

sections.what: The [current program](https://helpamericahear.org/help-america-hear-program) provides two prescription hearing aids, custom molds and one year of limited service for eligible people with moderate to profound hearing loss. It screens income, assets, insurance and alternatives. A $250 deposit is applied to fitting if charged, or refundable when the clinician donates services; patients pay for evaluations, medical clearance, batteries and other excluded items. The [FAQ](https://helpamericahear.org/faq) still describes an application fee and a $36,000 income cap, while the current program page describes income tiers. Those discrepancies should be resolved from the current application, not blended into one rule. The [FY2025 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202620159349301802/IRS990) reports over 120 people receiving hearing aids/services and a separate scholarship program.
sections.monitoring: The return provides service counts but no linked hearing thresholds, completion denominator, device-use logs, hearing handicap scores or long-term utility outcomes. [Schedule M](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202620159349301802/IRS990ScheduleM) records 164 contributed hearing-aid items valued at $123,000; that is not 164 newly treated people or a matched cohort of bilateral fittings. The [current site](https://helpamericahear.org/) describes events and scholarships but mixes current and older dates. Provider follow-up is useful, yet the [FAQ](https://helpamericahear.org/faq) offers only 3–5 visits or up to one year, depending on the provider. Sustained use, repairs, access barriers and replacement after that year determine health durability. The same ‘over 120’ wording appears in all three reviewed returns; it is not a reconciled annual fitting cohort.
sections.qualitative: The [ACHIEVE communication analysis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39266468/) found a roughly 9-point advantage on the 40-point hearing-handicap scale through three years. [Placebo-controlled US research](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28252160/) also supports genuine hearing benefit. A [Singapore delayed-start trial](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7709244/) estimated a 0.12 HUI utility difference at three months, but used selected volunteers, a modified scoring procedure and assumed long-term use. In contrast, [ACHIEVE's generic RAND-36 analysis](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2826555) found no significant physical or mental composite benefit. We therefore test a smaller 0.04 annual utility improvement without treating it as an observed recipient effect. The [primary cognition trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37478886/) was null overall despite subgroup differences; no dementia prevention or mortality gain is credited.
sections.cost: Cost per 10 USA QALYs is not estimated because the next-dollar rate of additional completed fittings is unknown. A transparent conditional case uses $3,000 of recipient support per fitted patient, 60% funding/capacity additionality, 70% benefit not available elsewhere, 75% sustained use and four years of benefit. It yields about $690,000 per 10 USA QALYs; an efficient favorable case is about $22,000, while short use and weak benefit can produce no net gain. These are tests, not a bounded positive estimate. At the conditional clinical assumptions, a $1 million threshold requires at least 41% financing/capacity additionality at $3,000 per case. A donation that only replaces existing sponsor funding or sits behind a fixed provider quota may create no additional fittings.
sections.funding:
The [FY2025 original return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202620159349301802/IRS990) shows $278,776 functional expense plus $147,746 direct fundraising-event costs, giving $426,522 gross accounting expense. Removing $123,000 recorded donated aids gives a $303,522 non-in-kind expense proxy, not cash flow or marginal cost. Functional spending includes $40,000 scholarships. Event net income excludes $194,060 event contributions: adding those to $45,380 event receipts and subtracting direct costs gives $91,694 before other fundraising expenses, so the negative net-event line alone does not show a loss-making event. Revenue less functional expense was −$15,225 and unrestricted net assets $71,754. Small reserves support possible funding need, but do not establish available extra donated devices or clinicians. Original Medicare [does not cover aids](https://www.medicare.gov/coverage/hearing-aids); other coverage and charity programs may. [OTC aids](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/hearing-aids/otc-hearing-aids-what-you-should-know) are intended for adults with mild-to-moderate loss, not a universal alternative for this program's population.

A [secondary index](https://www.causeiq.com/organizations/foundation-for-sight-and-sound,200878279/) includes a California registration flag that has not been resolved against the original registry. This does not establish national closure or ineligibility. We withhold a donation recommendation and checkout button until the relevant status is clarified; the research model is not legal or tax advice.

model.costScope: Ordinary unrestricted recipient support, with all recipient fundraising, operations and scholarships retained in the planning cost. G=$10,000 is normalization only. c=$3,000 is a conditional full-support cash-cost prior anchored to gross expenses less identifiable donated aids divided by a conservative120-patient denominator; this ratio is not a verified production function. Patient tests, travel and fitting costs and donated provider/device resource costs are separately disclosed, not claimed free to society.
model.geographicAttribution: Official program and return describe nationwide domestic services and no foreign operations. Conditional g=.99 allows incidental nonresident benefit; range.98–1. USA includes residents of50states and DC. Headquarters location and citizenship are not allocation keys.
model.formula: D=sum[t=1..T]((1−m)/1.03)^t. N=(G/c)×b. Q_all=N×(s×u×p×D−h). Q_USA=Q_all×g. Price per10=10G/Q_USA only if positive. b is financing/provider/manufacturer additionality; s is benefit not otherwise obtained; p is sustained effective use; u is utility gain while using devices. h is an adverse-burden allowance retained for all additional fittings even when s=0. Main result is null because b and current marginal c are not empirically bounded.
model.counterfactual: The financial screen makes otherwise-unmet need plausible but does not prove no alternative care. s allows Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, veterans' programs, other charities, family purchase or suitable OTC options. b separately discounts existing sponsorship, fixed donated-device quotas, provider slots and reserves. c includes failed applications/administration through the whole-recipient historical anchor; p discounts post-fitting use, not completion twice.
model.attribution: No extra hearing gain is credited to both scholarship and standard-program recipients. Scholarship cash and awareness receive no assumed health benefit but remain in cost; their separate benefits are unquantified. Each recipient is counted once, not once per device. Clinical priors transfer from external trials with better follow-up, not from device retail values. The main uncertainty is donation-sensitive completed care, so numerical cases are conditional and do not establish a favorable bound.
model.uncertainty: Hearing-specific function improves in randomized studies, but QALY measurement is sensitive to instrument and population. The Singapore .12 utility difference is not adopted directly. Age, hearing loss severity, fitting quality, ongoing use, repair access and alternatives could materially change benefit. The current program's manufacturer/provider constraint is missing; setting b=.6 is a scenario, not an estimated probability.
model.nativeOutcomes: The FY2025 return repeats an over-120 people/services narrative also present in earlier returns; this is not a verified annual cohort. It separately lists 164 donated device items, a different unit. Gross expense $426,522 minus $123,000 noncash aids equals $303,522, or $2,529.35 using a hypothetical 120-recipient denominator: a rough cost diagnostic, not an observed annual cost per patient. Conditional c=$3,000 and b=0.6 imply two additional fitted patients per arithmetic unit; net clinical QALYs per such patient are approximately 0.0733 before geography.

sensitivity: At conditional clinical inputs and c=$3000, achieving$1million per10 requires b≥.4135; achieving$100000 requires b≥4.135, impossible. Lower costs or larger sustained clinical benefit are required for the tighter threshold.
At b=.6 and other conditional inputs, c must be≤$4353 for$1million per10 or≤$435 for$100000 per10. A free manufacturer device alone does not establish either full-support cost.

At c3000 and b.6, annual effective-use utility u must be≥.02773 for$1million per10 or≥.27248 for$100000. Generic quality-of-life nulls make the former uncertain; the latter exceeds the adopted hearing-utility evidence.
Without current funding-sensitive completed fittings, the main price stays unestimated even though a conditional model is calculable. Zero manufacturer/provider capacity expansion means b=0.

Adding$1325 percase as an illustrative resource allowance for donated devices and external fitting/testing support increases the conditional social-cost price by44%, to about$993000 per10. This is not a procurement quote; actual donated opportunity cost and patient expenses are missing.
Reducing benefit to one year, or substantial failure to obtain replacement/repairs after the included service year, erodes most of the four-year gain.
No dementia, survival, earnings or scholarship-value addition is made. Communication points and device market values cannot be added to QALYs.
Current webpage deposit terms and FAQ fee/income language conflict. If up-front costs exclude the poorest or reduce completed care, historical referral counts overstate reachable benefit.

Case-mix and current donation allocation could differ from historical120-person volume. The whole-recipient model intentionally retains event and scholarship costs instead of pricing only the best donated-device episode.

reports.program: Affordable mail-order medicines, free-medication assistance and clinic support

acceptance.evidence: docs/geography-access-batch-five-acceptance.md; independent Medium audit plus root review; research only.

what: Rx Outreach operates a nonprofit mail-order pharmacy with low cash prices and free standard delivery.
It also provides separately funded medication assistance, including Fill the Gap for eligible older adults around St. Louis.
Its promising health mechanism is preventing clinically important treatment gaps, not simply selling more prescriptions.
strengths: Existing pharmacy infrastructure can reach patients and clinics without a general income application or insurance requirement.
Randomized free-medicine studies support a real adherence mechanism, especially when cost prevents necessary treatment.
Original financial schedules separate purchased medicines from donated inventory, making financial claims inspectable.
reservations: Additional human patient-years caused by an unrestricted donation, rather than earned revenue or partner funding, are not measured.
Medication class, patient risk, sustained use and realistic alternatives determine health yield; shipment totals cannot establish a QALY estimate.
Territorial and pet prescriptions are outside this human USA boundary, while current finances lag a changing pharmacy model.

sections.what: The [current general pharmacy](https://rxoutreach.org/patients/) requires an available medication and valid prescription, not an income application, membership or insurance. Its [clinic service](https://rxoutreach.org/why_clinics/) supports patient-pay, clinic-pay and hybrid arrangements and can ship to a clinic for people without secure housing. [Fill the Gap](https://rxoutreach.org/fill-the-gap/) separately offers covered medicines free to eligible adults aged 55 or older, at or below 300% of the federal poverty level, in the St. Louis region; meeting eligibility does not guarantee enrollment. Current criteria allow insured patients and should not be replaced with older launch restrictions. Other [assistance pathways](https://rxoutreach.org/patient-assistance-programs/) include disaster relief and a Blue Circle Health partnership. An ordinary donation supports this mixed recipient, not exclusively the strongest free-medication pathway.
sections.monitoring: A [dated 2024 overview](https://rxoutreach.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/Printable-RxO-Two-Pager-2.18.25.pdf) reports 34,740 unique patients, 188,993 shipped prescriptions and 2,534 facilities/clinics. Its geographic statement includes all 50 states, DC, Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands. These are delivery outputs, not additional treatment or health outcomes. The [current donor page](https://rxoutreach.org/donors-supporters/) instead gives a loose 120,000-plus annual prescription claim without a reporting year; it is not a like-for-like trend. No usable recipient-level comparison of medication persistence, disease control, admissions or utility was found in this bounded review. A next evaluation should link human recipient-years, drug class, baseline cost-related nonadherence, alternative coverage, fills, actual use, harms and outcomes. [Pet prescriptions](https://rxoutreach.org/pets/) need a separate denominator.
sections.qualitative: [CLEAN Meds](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8139488/) randomized 786 Canadian primary-care patients reporting cost-related nonadherence. Free essential medicines improved appropriate adherence by 10.1 percentage points at two years, but available diabetes, blood-pressure and lipid outcomes were not statistically different; missing clinical measurements limit interpretation. Its [one-year findings](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6784757/) included better blood pressure, illustrating why a short-term surrogate should not be assumed permanent. The US [MI-FREEE trial](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMsa1107913) improved adherence by 4–6 points after myocardial infarction; the primary vascular-event/revascularization outcome was not significantly reduced, although a secondary first-major-vascular-event rate was 11.0 versus 12.8 per 100 person-years. [ARTEMIS](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2720024) likewise improved medication persistence without a significant one-year cardiovascular-event reduction. These studies support plausibility, not a universal shipment-to-health multiplier. Our judgment is that targeted prevention of high-risk treatment interruption merits further diligence; the unrestricted recipient is not yet demonstrated to have unusually high health yield.
sections.cost: Cost per 10 USA QALYs is not estimated. The [2024 return](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202531989349100408/IRS990PF) implies about $401 of gross recipient expense per reported unique patient, or $74 per shipment. Neither is the marginal cost of a full year of additional treatment. The model disclosure uses a $400 patient-year cost benchmark and 50% funding additionality only to make thresholds concrete: reaching $1 million per 10 USA QALYs would require about 0.0082 net QALYs per additional patient-year before a 98% USA share; the $100,000 threshold requires about 0.082. Under an illustrative, attenuated [post-MI mechanism](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMsa1107913), the former requires roughly 48% of additional patient-years to have that high-risk clinical profile when each prevented event preserves two discounted QALYs. This is a question for measurement, not an estimate that 48% actually do. Other disease benefits remain unquantified.
sections.funding: Original Form 990-PF book expenses were [$12,368,983 in 2022](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202331939349100408/IRS990PF), [$21,535,029 in 2023](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202402299349100110/IRS990PF) and [$13,936,912 in 2024](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202531989349100408/IRS990PF), averaging about $15.95 million. The [2024 expense schedule](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202531989349100408/OtherExpensesSchedule) already includes $3,132,063 of purchased drug costs, $2,610,784 of in-kind inventory and $79,473 of other in-kind expense; do not add drug costs again. Removing only identified in-kind expenses leaves a $11,246,655 non-in-kind expense proxy, not cash flow. The corresponding proxies rose from $7.12 million in 2022 and $9.05 million in 2023: the gross decline does not show improved efficiency. In 2024, prescription revenue was $10,516,967, contributions $2,892,140 and the book deficit $516,395. Year-end unrestricted net assets were $1,640,703, with $437,272 in savings/temporary cash investments; these are dated figures, not a current runway forecast. The 2026 [clinic page](https://rxoutreach.org/why_clinics/) says nearly all inventory is now purchased directly, so prior donated-drug shares may be obsolete. [Deaconess's December 2025 award](https://deaconess.org/dec-2025-deaconess-awards-organizations-dedicated-to-youth-older-adults/) supports Fill the Gap expansion but does not establish an unfunded patient quota or matching leverage. A current budget, program-specific subsidy schedule, committed grants and waitlist are needed.

model.costScope: Unrestricted support to Rx Outreach Inc., EIN35-2378788. Recipient expenses include pharmacy procurement, dispensing, staff, systems, overhead and fundraising. Gross book expenses include in-kind inventory; c is unknown net recipient support needed per newly supported human patient-year, not retail drug value. Patient/clinic payments and sponsors can finance services without a new donation. Unmodeled pet services and other activities cannot be silently removed from the donation numerator. The cost of medication access borne by patients, providers or other funders is not free in a societal model; the reported donation skeleton does not claim total economic cost-effectiveness.
model.geographicAttribution: Human health of residents of 50 states plus DC. Observed 2024 service includes Puerto Rico and Virgin Islands, which are excluded. Current pet prescriptions are not human QALYs and require separate allocation before human patient-years. No outcome-weighted territorial share is available. g=.98 is a sensitivity benchmark only; current St. Louis Fill the Gap human patients would be within boundary, but unrestricted allocations are not all Fill the Gap.
model.formula: General skeleton: Q_USA = G × (b/c) × theta × g, where theta is net cumulative QALYs produced by one additional human patient-year of medication access, including later consequences discounted once. Inspectable post-MI test only: theta = f × e × t × q + z − h. f=share with trial-like high-risk post-MI prevention; e=0.018 fewer first major vascular events per patient-year (secondary MI-FREEE rate difference); t=transport/implementation attenuation; q=discounted net QALYs per event prevented; z=net health from other mechanisms; h=incremental adverse-treatment/access burden per supported human patient-year. Price = 10c/[b theta g] for positive theta. G=10000 merely normalizes disclosure arithmetic. No extra adherence multiplier is applied to e, which already measures intention-to-treat access effects.
model.counterfactual: Compare to the medication access patients would actually obtain through existing Rx Outreach sales, clinic subsidies, insurance, Medicare/Medicaid, manufacturer assistance or other cash pharmacies. [Current Medicare Part D](https://www.medicare.gov/health-drug-plans/part-d/basics/costs) has a $2,100 2026 covered-drug out-of-pocket cap, while [Cost Plus Drugs](https://www.markcubancostplusdrugcompany.com/) supplies an alternative cash/mail-order channel. These do not eliminate all barriers, but old retail sticker-price savings are not the counterfactual. An unrestricted gift could subsidize already-paid fills, replace renewed grant support, finance marketing or sustain operations rather than add patient-years. b includes that financing additionality; t captures clinical transport, not the same funding discount.
model.attribution: Do not attribute all efficacy of a prescribed drug to the dispensing charity. Prescribers, patients, manufacturers, clinics and public/private payers contribute. The trial event contrast incorporates access-induced uptake/adherence rather than treatment efficacy in fully adherent patients. Pharmacy-specific clinical mix and the share of services actually expanded by philanthropy remain unknown; no claim of zero alternative care.
model.uncertainty: Main central value is null because b/c, theta and geographic human allocation are not jointly identified. Conditional values below are algebraic probes, not confidence bounds, a recipient expected value, or evidence that all other pathways have zero value. The post-MI trial's positive secondary endpoint coexists with a nonsignificant primary endpoint; t may be zero. q=2 is an explicit severity/lifetime judgment, not a measured Rx Outreach utility. A financial savings estimate is not a QALY. Access can also cause adverse effects or inappropriate treatment; h remains when modeled benefit is zero.

Unique people are not full patient-years, shipments have varying days supply and polypharmacy, and donated inventory fair values distort resource prices. Desired causal unit is additional appropriately treated human patient-year, separated by drug/risk class and alternative care.

reports.program: California clean-air policy, community monitoring and education

acceptance.evidence: docs/geography-evidence-batch-four-acceptance.md; root model/source/financial review; research only, not a qualified pick.

what: Coalition for Clean Air advocates for cleaner transportation and air policy across California and runs community monitoring and education projects.
Its current YMCA project combines air-quality measurements with upgraded filtration, while its policy work seeks broader emissions reductions.
The health return of an ordinary donation depends on additional exposure reduction beyond already-funded projects and existing rules.
strengths: Air pollution has a strong external health-evidence base, and statewide policy changes can reach many people.
Current monitoring reports document actual filter upgrades and continuing measurements rather than only campaign reach.
Recent original accounts make operating scale, spending mix and financial deterioration inspectable.
reservations: No marginal spending plan connects an extra donation to additional exposure reduction or a policy probability change.
Indoor-versus-outdoor filtration percentages are not improvements against the no-upgrade counterfactual, and monitoring alone is not health.
Government grants, sponsors, existing regulations, legal reversals and benefits outside California complicate additionality and scope.

sections.what:
Coalition for Clean Air, EIN 23-7120567, is the California nonprofit, not the similarly named international Climate and Clean Air Coalition or Pennsylvania Clean Air Council. Ordinary gifts fund its mix of policy advocacy, community projects, education and support costs. Current priorities include freight emissions, clean transportation investment and community air protection. [Current organization](https://www.ccair.org/) [Donation recipient](https://ccair.app.neoncrm.com/forms/donate)

The original FY 2025 return describes education, advocacy, monitoring and work with schools and community organizations as a combined program. It does not provide a marginal allocation that would justify treating a general donation as a dedicated filtration or truck-repair grant. [Original return](https://www.ccair.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2024-2025-CCA-Form-990.pdf)
sections.monitoring:
AirAware is an EPA-funded partnership with TD Enviro, IQAir and three YMCAs. Its first annual report establishes pre-upgrade conditions and records Corona-Norco’s September 4, 2025 MERV-8 to MERV-16 upgrade. The reported 91% reduction is relative to outdoor concentration, not a 91% causal reduction from the old indoor exposure. [Project](https://www.ccair.org/projects/airaware-ymcas/) [Baseline report](https://www.ccair.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/AirAware2025_1stAnnualAirQualityReport.pdf)

The current quarterly report still finds effective filtration, but excludes two rooms from a higher-pollution-day comparison because of missing data and identifies indoor pollution spikes despite filtration. It includes observations through July 6 despite an April–June label and July 1 filename; no publication day is inferred from the filename. It discusses moving a monitor after the grant ends in October. That is a concrete continuation question, not proof that an unrestricted gift would otherwise buy replacement filters. [Current quarterly report](https://www.ccair.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/2026.07.01_Corona-Norco-YMCA-Y2Q2-Report.pdf)

Measure additional occupied person-hours at a given concentration reduction, maintenance and energy costs, equipment uptime and the no-gift replacement plan. For policy, measure changed implementation probability or compliance, emissions, dispersion and population-weighted exposure—not pledges, monitors, budget dollars or the total population covered by a rule.
sections.qualitative:
The health mechanism is credible, but its transfer requires care. A Medicare cohort study found a 7.3% mortality association per 10 micrograms/m³ higher long-term PM 2.5, with important age, pollution-mixture and residual-confounding limitations. [Di study](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1702747) A later analysis of 68.5 million enrollees used several causal-inference approaches; its most conservative full-cohort hazard ratio was 1.06 per 10 micrograms/m³. Causal interpretation still requires adequate confounder control. Neither study directly estimates health gains from a few hours in a YMCA, especially for children. [Wu study](https://xiaowu.io/publication/wu2020evaluating/wu2020evaluating.pdf)

Historical policy success is not a new gift’s return. CARB projects large Clean Truck Check benefits and its current guidance says testing requirements remain in effect. Those existing benefits belong in the no-new-donation counterfactual unless a specific marginal enforcement or protection role is shown. [Program](https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/our-work/programs/CTC/about) [Current requirements](https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/our-work/programs/inspection-and-maintenance-program/hd-im-fact-sheets) CCA’s June 2026 budget statement supports further public spending, but does not identify a donation-sensitive probability of obtaining it. Its 2025 locomotive-rule repeal comment illustrates legal fragility rather than guaranteed permanent policy gains. [Budget statement](https://www.ccair.org/statement-coalition-for-clean-air-supports-2026-state-budget-deal-to-fund-clean-cars-trucks-and-buses-and-community-air-protection/) [Repeal comment](https://www.ccair.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/CCA-Comment-letter-on-Loco-Rule-Repeal-6.16.25.pdf)
sections.cost:
The original returns show comparable June-year-end expenses of $1,403,245 in FY 2023, $2,089,892 in FY 2024 and $2,452,895 in FY 2025, averaging $1,982,010.67. This consistent Form 990 Part IX presentation includes all program and support functions but excludes direct event expenses netted against event revenue; FY 2025 excludes $42,017 that way. The donation model itself uses the entire gift as cost. [FY 2024 return and comparison](https://www.ccair.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/2023-CCA-Form-990.pdf) [FY 2025 return](https://www.ccair.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2024-2025-CCA-Form-990.pdf)

No central price is assigned. An explicit survival-based threshold instead asks how much additional exposure reduction would be needed. For an illustrative older-adult population with annual mortality hazard 0.05 and utility 0.75, apply the external hazard ratio 1.06 per 10 micrograms/m³ to a sustained 1 microgram/m³ reduction for ten years, discounting at 3%. Integrating the difference between the two survival curves gives 0.00653294 QALY per person within that finite window. Thus about 153 or 1,531 additional people receiving that ten-year reduction per $100,000 would meet $1 million or $100,000 per 10 QALYs. These are algebraic requirements, not a CCA forecast, a plausible interval or a claim about YMCA participants. The normalization is arithmetic, not a proposed grant.

A credible estimate needs the gift-induced exposure change and affected population, not an arbitrary fraction of CARB’s total projected deaths. Count pollution and climate pathways separately, excluding non-California health from this edition and avoiding overlap between mortality and morbidity. Government spending, vehicle replacement, electricity, maintenance and partner resources also matter for gross societal cost.
sections.funding:
FY 2025 revenue was $2,149,048, $303,847 below reported expenses. Program, management and fundraising expenses were $1,479,082, $647,639 and $326,174. Consultants accounted for $974,336; salaries and benefits totaled $1,019,943. Year-end net assets were $1,113,614, including $1,036,114 without donor restrictions. Fee-for-service contracts generated $321,468. [Original return](https://www.ccair.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2024-2025-CCA-Form-990.pdf)

The deficit makes a current funding plan important, but does not establish a productive unrestricted gap by itself. The public project description explicitly identifies EPA support, so an ordinary gift might extend, substitute for or support work outside that grant. The original return does not isolate a current dollar cost per additional filter installation or successful policy intervention. Ask which consultant or staff capacity, maintenance or implementation work is unfunded; whether restricted grants, sponsors, equipment partners or reserves would otherwise cover it; and what measured exposure reduction would result. [Financial index](https://www.ccair.org/about/financial/) [Project funding](https://www.ccair.org/projects/airaware-ymcas/)

model.costScope: Full ordinary recipient cash gift across programs and support; historical Part IX expense scale consistently excludes netted direct event expenses. Additional government, fleet, equipment, electricity and partner resources required for a gross-resource calculation.
model.geographicAttribution: Integrate health gained while beneficiaries are inside the California edition boundary. California projects do not make all climate or transported air-pollution benefits California benefits. Reference threshold is restricted to California exposure and health time, g=1 by construction.
model.formula: For person/group j, Q_CA(C)=sum_j N_j * integral_0^T [u1_j(t)*S1_j(t;DeltaPM(C*a*f),other causes)-u0_j(t)*S0_j(t)]*g_j(t)/(1.03)^t dt, plus non-overlapping morbidity effects minus harms. Policy branch weights conditional exposure paths by gift-induced change in implementation probability, not arbitrary coalition share. Reference: beta=ln(1.06)/10; h0=.05; h1=h0*exp(-beta*1); u=.75; rho=ln(1.03); T=10; q=u*[(1-exp(-(h1+rho)*T))/(h1+rho)-(1-exp(-(h0+rho)*T))/(h0+rho)]=.006532944220465575. Price=10*C/Q_CA if Q_CA>0.
model.counterfactual: Existing grants, planned YMCA upgrades, partner work, statutory testing and public budgets continue absent the new gift. Measure only extra duration, coverage, compliance, policy probability or exposure reduction. A monitor that reveals pollution without changing exposure yields no health in this branch.
model.attribution: Donation allocation and funding additionality enter the exposure or policy mechanism. Do not credit CCA with every benefit of a regulation it supported, or multiply a causal probability change by a second coalition-share haircut. Joint exposure/survival paths prevent repeated annual deaths and overlapping policy benefits being counted as separate lifetime rescues.
model.uncertainty: Central unknown because marginal gift-to-exposure or policy yield is not identified. Reference survival arithmetic is explicitly judgment-based outside its external hazard ratio, and is not a bounded forecast. The absence of an estimate is not evidence of zero value; zero and adverse effects remain possible.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional population-weighted PM2.5 exposure reduction in micrograms/m³-person-years, calibrated to occupied time and counterfactual filtration; implemented emissions changes with dispersion; finite survival and morbidity trajectories. Monitors, AQI categories, pledges and nominal budgets are not health units.

sensitivity: If effects are credited only within one year, q falls to 0.0001033373 QALY per reference person; the threshold population rises about 63-fold. This truncates later survival benefit rather than assuming it never exists.

A policy producing the reference exposure reduction for 100,000 people conditional on success would need a gift-induced success-probability increase of 0.0015307 or 0.0153070 for the two thresholds. That footprint is an illustration, not a measured CCA opportunity.

Scale utility from 0.75 to 0.5 and threshold population increases by 50%. Changing mortality hazard or exposure-response transfer requires recalculating survival curves, not adding lifetime QALYs to each annual avoided death.

YMCA occupancy is only part of a person's day; annual whole-person exposure change is not equal to the room concentration change. Do not apply elderly mortality coefficients to child participants without an age-specific bridge.

Quarterly indoor/outdoor differences can reflect changing outdoor pollution, occupancy and indoor sources. Estimate the no-upgrade indoor counterfactual and maintenance persistence before using them as effects.
Full global climate benefits are outside this California calculation. A social denominator includes incremental public and private implementation resources, not just charitable dollars.

Incremental societal costs, geographic spillovers, harms and overlap across pollution, climate and clinical outcomes.
